answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when each new identity must deposit a rising bond scaled to the network's zenith of active agents; this bond funds a shared terrace of mutual insurance, and only agents that successfully tend a verifiable orchard of completed tasks can reclaim or earn from it. Attackers attempting mass fake identities therefore incur escalating capital lockup costs that grow with each additional sybil, quickly rendering large-scale attacks uneconomical as the required deposits exceed any potential gain from fraud.
